From: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com

Hi Ellen —

Thanks for the SOW and clear questions. High level answers below; attached is a compact SLA matrix that maps crediting behavior and pricing impact.

1) Flex credits: monthly aggregate pool with a per-incident floor. Practically, that means credits are accrued against the monthly SLAs and applied to the invoice as a single line item. Individual incidents will never exceed 25% of the month’s total credits to avoid abuse.

2) Zonal fallback & on-call billing:
   - Automated regional failover (no manual intervention): no billable on-call hours; this is covered under our standard redundancy operations.
   - Manual escalation requiring runbook execution: billed at the retainer rate for the first 2 hours; beyond that, standard T&M applies per the retainer schedule. If an incident crosses zones due to a cascading failure, we prorate hours based on time spent per region.

3) Pricing example (ballpark):
   - Baseline: 99.9% uptime, business hours triage only — $X,XXX/month (existing commit)
   - Blended 99.95% + 24/7 retainer (24/7 on-call, priority routing, 30-minute P1 response): incremental ~ +28% on the committed monthly retainer; estimated additional $2,400/month for their current footprint. See attached matrix for line-item math.

We can soften that with a 9-12 month commit and offer a 10% discount on the retainer. If they prefer incident-level credits instead of monthly pooling, we can allow that for a 15% uplift on the retainer.

Next steps: if you’re aligned we’ll produce a redline to the SOW that includes the blended uptime band and the retainer appendix.

Best,
Vivek
---End Customer Draft---

Numbers: I pulled NovaBay's committed baseline from CRM and the usage shows steady token consumption (approx 2.2M inference tokens/month; translated to 0.9 GPU-month equivalent). That’s the basis for the $2.4k delta above. Karthik — confirm the math and I’ll sign off.

— Laura

Thanks for the fast turnaround and clear options. Procurement reviewed the numbers. A couple follow-ups before we proceed:
- The 25% per-incident cap on monthly credits — can that be (a) raised to 35% for critical incidents only, and (b) gated by a 2-person exec sign-off?
- We’d like the 9-month commit + 10% retainer discount. If you can include the one-month onboarding credit and a clause that the retainer price is fixed for 12 months, we can move to signature.

Subject: Re: Flexible SLA credits + on-call fallback questions — agreed terms
\Ellen / Tony —

Thanks — we can agree to the requested changes with the following confirmation:

1) Incident cap: raise to 35% for incidents classified as P1 Critical (definition: total regional outage impacting >50% of requests for >15 minutes); P1 critical incidents will require two exec contacts to authorize a credit beyond the standard cap.
2) Pricing & discount: 9-month commit with 10% off the retainer, plus a one-month onboarding credit applied to the first invoice. Retainer price fixed for 12 months from execution.
3) Cross-zone proration language for legal (drop-in): "If a manual escalation requires intervention across multiple regions, billable on-call hours will be prorated to the region(s) where manual actions occurred. Proration will be calculated on a time-in-region basis and documented in the incident report; total billed hours will exclude automated failover intervals."

We will produce a redlined SOW and an addendum that captures the retainer appendix and crediting mechanics. I’ll send the DocuSign link and the redline by EOD. If you’re both available tomorrow at 10am PT we can do a short signoff call.

Best,
Vivek
VP, Sales — Redwood Inference
